record.title: Is there a prime between n^(2)and (n+1)^(2 )for every n > 0
record.statement: Erdős: Is there a prime between n^(2)and (n+1)^(2 )for every n > 0?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős)

record.title: Let f be the formal power series over Z/2Z whose nth coefficient is the parity of the divisor function Ă_(0)(n)
record.statement: /Riasanovsky: Let f be the formal power series over Z/2Z whose nth coefficient is the parity of the divisor function Ă_(0)(n). Is it true that the density of 1's in the power series 1/f is 1/32?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Riasanovsky)

record.title: Small components of subharmonic level sets
record.statement: Let subharmonic functions $u_k$ on the unit square converge uniformly to $u(x,y)=x$. If $D_k=\{u_k<0\}$ and $D_k^*$ is the component containing $-1/2$, can $D_k\setminus D_k^*$ meet every horizontal segment $[-1+it,1+it]$, $-1<t<1$?
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Defect relation for points in $\mathbb P^2$
record.statement: Let $f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb P^2$ be linearly nondegenerate and let $\delta(a,f)$ be the Nevanlinna deficiency of a point $a\in\mathbb P^2$. Prove that for every system of points in general position, $$\sum_a\delta(a,f)\le1.$$
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Packing reciprocal rectangles in a square
record.statement: For every positive integer $k$, let $R_k$ be a $1/k$ by $1/(k+1)$ rectangle. Can the entire collection $(R_k)_{k\ge1}$ be packed without overlap into the unit square?
record.source_name: Eppstein - The Geometry Junkyard: Open Problems (proposed by David Eppstein and cited proposers)

record.title: Log-concave measures
record.statement: For Ollivier's coarse Ricci curvature, smooth uniformly strictly log-concave measures on $\mathbb{R}^N$ have positive curvature. What can be said for a general log-concave measure? In particular, analyze a convex body equipped with Brownian motion conditioned not to leave it.
record.source_name: Ollivier - Discrete Ricci curvature: Open problems (2008) (proposed by Yann Ollivier)

record.title: Isoperimetric profile and curvature at infinity
record.statement: Suppose the global infimum of coarse Ricci curvature is zero, while its infimum on every finite-radius ball about an origin is positive. Is there a systematic relation between the rate at which curvature tends to zero at infinity and the isoperimetric profile? Analyze, for example, the $M/M/k$ queue.
record.source_name: Ollivier - Discrete Ricci curvature: Open problems (2008) (proposed by Yann Ollivier)

record.title: Fractal caustics
record.statement: Are there geodesic flows or Birkhoff billiards with fractal caustics? More specifically, for every $1\leq s<2$, is there a caustic of a convex billiard with Hausdorff dimension $s$; and for every $s\geq1$, is there a Riemannian manifold $M$ and a point whose caustic has Hausdorff dimension $s$?
record.source_name: Knill - Open problems in Hamiltonian dynamics (2000) (proposed by Oliver Knill)

record.title: Periodic orbits
record.statement: (a) Is the set of $n$-periodic orbits of a smooth strictly convex Birkhoff billiard nowhere dense for every $n$? (b) Does every polygonal Birkhoff billiard have a periodic orbit?
record.source_name: Knill - Open problems in Hamiltonian dynamics (2000)

record.title: Equal-entropy factors conjecture
record.statement: Let $A,B$ be irreducible integer matrices of the same spectral radius. Suppose $\operatorname{tr}(A^n)>0$ implies $\operatorname{tr}(B^n)>0$ for every $n$, and the dimension module of $B$ is a quotient of a closed submodule of that of $A$. Prove that the shift $S_B$ is a factor of $S_A$.
record.source_name: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

record.title: Commuting powers conjecture
record.statement: If $S$ and $T$ are mixing shifts of finite type, prove that $S^i$ and $T^j$ can commute for all sufficiently large integers $i,j$.
record.source_name: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

record.title: Full-support invariant measures
record.statement: For the symbolic system $X$ constructed in Section 14 of the source from a commuting pair of full-shift endomorphisms, is Haar measure its only invariant ergodic Borel probability measure with full support?
record.source_name: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

record.title: Growth of jointly periodic points II
record.statement: With $\nu(f,S_N)$ defined as in Question 25.3, must every surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton satisfy $\nu(f,S_N)\ge\sqrt N$?
record.source_name: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

record.title: Surjunctive groups
record.statement: Characterize the countable groups $G$ for which every injective $G$-equivariant cellular automaton on $A^G$, for every finite alphabet $A$, is surjective.
record.source_name: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

record.title: A Markus–Yamabe/La Salle problem for discrete dynamical systems
record.statement: Let $F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be smooth, have a fixed point, and satisfy $$\rho\bigl(|DF(x)|\bigr)<1\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^2.$$ Is the fixed point globally asymptotically stable?
record.source_name: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

record.title: Conjecture of multiplicative persistence
record.statement: For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Pi(n)$ be the product of its decimal digits, and let $\operatorname{Pm}(n)$ be the least positive integer such that $\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)}(n)=\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)+1}(n)$. Is $\operatorname{Pm}(n)\leq11$ for every $n$?
record.source_name: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

record.title: The 196 conjecture
record.statement: Define $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ by $f(n)=n+\operatorname{rev}(n)$, where $\operatorname{rev}$ reverses the decimal digits. Are there infinitely many $n$ for which no iterate $f^k(n)$, $k>0$, is a palindrome? Is the least such $n$ equal to $196$?
record.source_name: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

record.title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 18
record.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T_1,\ldots, T_\ell)$ be a system and $\{p_1,\ldots, p_\ell\}$ be a family of intersective integer polynomials. Show that for every set $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ one has $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $n\in\mathbb N$.
record.source_name: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

record.title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 21
record.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a probability space, $T_1,\ldots, T_\ell \colon X\to X$ be invertible measure preserving transformations, and $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ we have $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{m+p_1(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{m+p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $m,n\in \mathbb N$.
record.source_name: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

record.title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 24
record.statement: Let $a,b$ be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$, we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N f(T^{[n^a]}x) \cdot g(T^{[n^b]}x)=\int f \ d\mu \cdot \int g\ d\mu $$ for almost every $x\in X$.
record.source_name: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

record.title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 33
record.statement: Suppose that $a,b\in(0,1)$ and $a\neq b$. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T,S)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$ we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(\omega)}f\cdot S^{b_n(\omega)}g= \mathbb E(f|\mathcal{I}_T)\cdot \mathbb E(g|\mathcal{I}_S) $$ where the limit is taken in $L^2(\mu)$ or pointwise.
record.source_name: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

record.title: Thurston's algorithm without critical finiteness
record.statement: Starting with an orientation-preserving branched covering $f_0:S^2\to S^2$ and three marked base points, iteratively conjugate it as in Thurston's pullback algorithm to obtain rational maps $r_n$ and coordinate maps $\phi_n$. Under what conditions does $r_n$ converge uniformly to a rational map $r_\infty$, and under what conditions and on what subset of $S^2$ does $\phi_n$ converge uniformly?
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

record.title: Periodic orbits near a Cremer point
record.statement: For a Cremer point of an arbitrary rational map, does every neighborhood contain infinitely many periodic orbits?
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

record.title: Local connectivity of real quadratic Julia sets
record.statement: For every real $c\in[-2,1/4]$, is the Julia set of $f_c(z)=z^2+c$ locally connected?
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

record.title: Uniform convergence to an irrationally indifferent fixed point
record.statement: Let $\varphi$ be a holomorphic germ fixing $z_0$ with multiplier $e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ for irrational $\alpha$. Can $\varphi^n(z)\to z_0$ uniformly on some domain?
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and Mikhail Lyubich)

record.title: Density of hyperbolic rational maps
record.statement: For every degree $d$, prove that expanding (hyperbolic, Axiom A) maps are dense in the spaces $\operatorname{Rat}_d$ of rational maps and $\operatorname{Poly}_d$ of polynomials.
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by Curt McMullen)

record.title: Effective computation of entropy for surface diffeomorphisms
record.statement: Given an explicitly specified smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $F$ of the $2$-sphere, is its topological entropy Turing-computable to arbitrary prescribed error, and can it be computed in useful time? Resolve this in particular for Hénon and standard-map families; in the area-preserving cases, ask the analogous question for measure-theoretic entropy.
record.source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

record.title: General Unfoldings of Nonconvex Polyhedra
record.statement: Can every closed polyhedron be cut along its surface and unfolded into one piece in the plane without overlap? Such an unfolding is called a general unfolding to distinguish from edge-unfoldings (see Problem 9) and vertex-unfoldings (see Problem 42).
record.source_name: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

record.title: Transforming Polygons via Vertex-Centroid Moves
record.statement: Given an arbitrary polygon, transform it by a finite sequence of ``vertex-centroid'' moves to a regular polygon. A vertex-centroid move is a translation of a vertex $v$ along the line $vm$, where $m$ is the centroid of the vertices of the polygon, i.e., $1/n$-th of the sum of the vertex coordinates. Vertices may move only one at a time, but in any order and any number of times.
record.source_name: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

record.title: Yao-Yao Graph a Spanner?
record.statement: Is the Yao-Yao Graph a $t$-spanner for constant $t$? A geometric graph is a $t$-spanner (or just a spanner) if, for every pair of nodes, the shortest distance between the nodes following the edges of the graph is at most $t$ times the Euclidean distance between them. See below for the definition of the Yao-Yao graph.
record.source_name: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 5
record.statement: What can be said about boundaries arising from strict hyperbolization constructions of Charney and Davis, [18]?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Nadia Benakli)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 7
record.statement: Suppose that Z is a compact metrizable topological space, G↷ Z is a convergence action which is topologically transitive, i.e. each G– orbit is dense in Z. Is there a Gromov-hyperbolic space X with the ideal boundary Z so that the action G ↷ Z extends to a uniformly quasi-isometric quasi-action G↷ X?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 12
record.statement: Can exotic homology manifolds as in [14] appear as ideal boundaries of Coxeter groups?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 15
record.statement: Suppose that ( N1, ∆1) and (N2, ∆2) are closed 3-manifolds equipped with ﬂag-triangulations, so that ∂∞C(N1, ∆1) = ∂∞C(N2, ∆2). Does it follow that every prime connected sum summand of Ni appears as a connected sum summand of Ni+1, i = 1, 2? What can be said in higher dimensions?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich, Tadeusz Januszkiewicz)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 16
record.statement: Let Z be a compactum which is a Z-boundary of a group G. Then Z is never a Boltyansky compactum. In the special case when Z is an Markov compactum, so that all building blocks Kσ → σ are isomorphic, it was proven in [29] that Z cannot be a Boltyansky compactum.
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Alexander Dranishnikov)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 17
record.statement: Examples of Kleiner and Croke [22], [23] of non-unique boundaries are badly non-locally-connected. Is that essential in having the “ﬂexibility” to have many boundaries? That is, does local connectedness imply uniqueness of the boundary (in the 1-ended case) for CAT(0) groups?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Kim Ruane)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 36
record.statement: Let f: Bn → Bn be a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Can f be approximated by globally quasiconformal diﬀeomorphisms fj: Bn → Bn? Can this be done so that fj’s are K-quasiconformal for all j?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 52
record.statement: Let G be a hyperbolic group. Is it true that G admit a uniformly quasiconformal discrete action on Sn (for some n)?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 66
record.statement: Is there an equivariant continuous map (called Cannon–Thurston map) from the unit circle S1 (the ideal boundary of G as an abstract group) to S2? Then Problem 64 is equivalent to 66.
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 67
record.statement: Let H ⊂ G be a hyperbolic subgroup of a hyperbolic group (we do not assume that H is quasiconvex). Is it true that there exists an equivariant continuous map ∂∞H → ∂∞G. See [46] for partial results in this direction.
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Mahan Mitra)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 68
record.statement: What is the Poisson boundary of the free group with an arbitrary measure?
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Vadim Kaimanovich)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 69
record.statement: There almost surely exists a horofunction h such that lim n→∞ − 1 n h(xn) = A, where A = lim n→∞ 1 n d(x0, xn). A theorem of Karlsson states that ∀ϵ > 0 there exists a horofunction hϵ such that A − ϵ ≤ − 1 n hϵ(xn) ≤ A + ϵ for all n ≥ N (ϵ).
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Conjecture of Anders Karlsson)

record.title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 87
record.statement: Prove that every arithmetic lattice in Isom( Hn) ( n ≥ 4) is non-coherent. See [38] for some partial results in this direction. It is well-known that every lattice in Isom( HHn) ( n ≥ 2) has Property T.
record.source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by M. Kapovich, L. Potyagailo, E.B. Vinberg)

record.title: Scalar Curvature Question [?16]: Singularities are Unstable
record.statement: Conjecture. Singularities are Unstable. Brian White told me about 30 years ago that he believed that Volume minimising hypersurfaces in generic Riemannian manifoldsX are non-singular: singularities disappear under arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of metrics inX. This was conﬁrmed in 1993 by Nathan Smale, [118] forn= 8, which extends the Schoen-Yau theorem ton= 8.
record.source_name: Gromov - 101 Questions, Problems and Conjectures around Scalar Curvature (2017) (proposed by Misha Gromov)

record.statement: For instance, letX be homomorphic to CP 2 and letvol(Uδ(S)) ≥δ2 for allT(X)-non-spin surfacesS ⊂X and 0<δ ≤1. Is then spin-area(X) ≥1/1 000 000?

record.title: Riemannian manifolds with curvature bounds
record.statement: For every $\ell,k>0$, there exist $C,L,K>0$ with the following effect. Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with injectivity radius $inj(M,g)\geq \ell$ and Ricci curvature $Ric(g)\geq k$. Then there exists a metric $h$ on $M$ with $inj(M,h)\geq L$ and $|Ric(h)|\leq K$ such that $$ \frac{1}{C}\,g\leq h\leq C\,g. $$
record.source_name: Morgan and Pansu - A List of Open Problems in Differential Geometry (2018) (proposed by Lashi Bandara, Universit\"at Potsdam, Germany)
